v1.feedback: The sumi-ink palette with amber dot accents is the strongest part — it genuinely reads as iki's cool/warm tension and the incense-rise motion earns its place. But 30 copies in concentric rings contradicts iki's core principle of restraint through suggestion; consider culling to center Lucy + one sparse ring (or fewer, larger satellites) so negative space does more work. The drape deformation at 0.18 rad max is nearly invisible — either commit to a visible vertical fold that reshapes the silhouette or drop it; half-measures read as unchanged parent. The stripe overlay modulating grey-to-slightly-darker-grey is too subtle to register as a graphic element — if you want Tanaka Ikko's bold graphic quality, the stripe needs to drive real contrast, not a 40% mix into near-identical values.

v2.feedback: The Tanaka Ikko graphic-stripe concept is a genuine morphing direction from the parent's selcouth aesthetic — the sumi/cream/vermillion palette is restrained and the bold vertical stripes read clearly on the Lucy silhouette. However the 'drape fold' displacement is too subtle at the current foldStrength to visibly reshape the silhouette as promised; crank it up or make the folds asymmetric so the figure actually looks draped rather than slightly wobbly. The four satellite copies at 0.42 scale are small enough to read as decorative clutter rather than compositional elements — either drop them or pull them closer and larger so they form a deliberate pattern. The vermillion dot accents on the floor plane compete with the figure's own dot highlights; simplify the floor to plain dark ground to let the striped Lucy command more visual weight.
